title: Willowleaf Podocarp: Ancient Podocarps You Can Visit
meta_description: A tropical conifer that never adopted the cone. One Rome specimen made Italy's register on rarity alone; the seed sits on a fleshy, bird-eaten stalk.
intro: Three of these stand on this site, two in Rome and one in Singapore, and each is protected for a different reason. Podocarps are a mostly southern conifer family that split off before pines existed and never adopted the cone: the seed sits instead on a swollen, fleshy stalk that turns purple and gets eaten by birds, which is how the species spread from the Himalayan foothills to New Guinea and why Buddhist communities planted it around temples across that range. Rome's Villa Sciarra specimen made Italy's national monumental register for a single reason, botanical rarity, with no claim to age or size at all; the city calls it splendid and enormous anyway. A second Rome tree, in Piazza Vittorio's garden, is one of the largest in the city and was listed in 2025. Singapore's grows on a lawn in the Botanic Gardens, its own age never recorded.
